summary.short: BIS interim final rule, effective 13 January 2025 (compliance from 15 May 2025), amending the Export Administration Regulations to require licences worldwide for advanced computing chips and for weights of closed AI models trained on 10^26 or more operations, with country compute allocations, new license exceptions and data-center VEU authorizations.
summary.long: The rule extends licensing of advanced computing chips (ECCN 3A090.a, 4A090.a and corresponding .z items) to all destinations and creates ECCN 4E091 for the parameters (weights) of AI models trained with 10^26 or more operations, excluding published weights and models less capable than the most advanced published model; foreign-direct-product rules reach foreign-produced items. License review is tiered by destination and headquarters: presumption of approval for 18 listed destinations plus the United States (Supplement No. 5 to part 740), presumption of denial for Country Group D:5 and Macau, and for all other destinations approval up to a per-country allocation of 790,000,000 TPP for 2025-2027 (raisable up to 100% with government assurances). New license exceptions: AIA (listed destinations, including model weights stored in secure facilities), ACM (development and production by private end users) and LPP (up to 26,900,000 TPP per consignee per year). Universal and National Data Center VEU authorizations carry compute caps (quarterly NVEU allocations; UVEU limits of 25%, 7% and 50% of compute outside listed countries) and conditions on ownership, supply chains, training location, model-weight storage, NIST 800-53/FedRAMP High security, personnel vetting and semi-annual reporting. Breaches may lead to revocation of VEU status and denial of licences.

territorial_scope.description: Applies to exports, reexports and in-country transfers of U.S.-origin and, through foreign direct product rules, foreign-produced advanced computing items and AI model weights to or within any destination worldwide, with treatment depending on the destination and on where the recipient or its ultimate parent is headquartered.

notes: Tiering: the regulatory text does not use the word 'tier'. Destinations are sorted into (i) the 18 destinations plus the United States listed in Supplement No. 5(a) to part 740 (presumption of approval; AIA; UVEU headquarters), (ii) Macau and Country Group D:5 (presumption of denial), and (iii) all other destinations (country allocation of 790,000,000 TPP for 2025-2027, then denial); Supplement No. 5(b) ('higher country allocation' with government assurances) lists no destinations in this text. Several treatments also turn on where an entity or its ultimate parent is headquartered. Ultimate consignees and VEU owners are coded as data_center_owner and VEU operators as data_center_operator, the closest roles in the vocabulary. TPP volume caps and triggers use the 'volume' variable; percentage compute caps use 'other'. NVEU allocation quarters are coded as phase_in_step events dated to the first month of each quarter ('2027 Q1–4' as 2027-01). Inconsistencies in the text: the AIA reporting trigger (§ 740.27(c)) and the LPP shipment notification (§ 740.29(g)(3)) state no operator ('of 253,000,000', 'of 3,200,000'), while the preamble says 'more than 3,200,000'; both coded as >=. § 740.27(c) refers to a notification 'described in (b)(4)' but § 740.27(b) ends at (b)(3); § 748.15(a)(2)(ii)(B) cites 'paragraph 6 or Supplement No. 10' (read as 'of'); § 740.29(g)(2) refers to 'License Exception TPP' (read as LPP); ECCN 4E091 Note 1 refers to 'Note 2' for the definition of training operations (Technical Note 2); Note 3 to 3A090 refers to 'Note 2 or 3 to 3A090', which are not reproduced in this text; § 748.3(f) says 'an average of widely used benchmarks' while ECCN 4E091 Note 2 says 'an aggregate'. The effective date is printed 'January 13. 2025'. The text gives the filing time (Filed 1-13-25) and the signatory (Assistant Secretary for Export Administration) but no signing date. Status: the registry records the instrument as repealed on the basis of a BIS press release of 2025-05-13 announcing rescission; this text does not mention rescission and no repealed event is coded (left for the resolve stage, which needs an official source such as a Federal Register rescission notice). Exemption for intentional publication: Supplement No. 10 states that none of its provisions apply to or prevent intentional publication of model weights, data or code.
